scenarios.stimulus: Reads in the upper half of the address space, below bit 31. After reset, with the bridge idle and no AW pending, send these supported reads one after another (ARCACHE=4'b0000, random ARID/ARPROT, RREADY always 1). (1) INCR, ARSIZE=2, ARLEN=3, ARADDR=0x7FFF_0010. (2) FIXED, ARSIZE=2, ARLEN=1, ARADDR=0x7FFF_0100. (3) WRAP, ARSIZE=2, ARLEN=3, ARADDR=0x7FFF_0024. (4) Single-beat INCR, ARSIZE=2, at ARADDR=0x0000_0100, so the beat address returns to the low region. None of these bursts crosses a 4-KiB boundary. The APB completer must answer every address, including 0x7FFF_xxxx, with PREADY after 0 to 2 wait cycles, PSLVERR=0 and a distinct PRDATA for each transfer. Use an address-agnostic responder or a memory model that covers this region, not the default error completer. Let the bridge go back to APB idle between transactions.

Writes in the upper half of the address space, below bit 31. After reset, with the bridge idle and no AR pending, send these supported writes one after another (AWCACHE=4'b0001, random AWID/AWPROT, BREADY always 1). Each AW is followed by exactly AWLEN+1 W beats, with WLAST only on the last beat and a full WSTRB=4'b1111 for word beats. (1) INCR, AWSIZE=2, AWLEN=3, AWADDR=0x7FFF_0010. (2) FIXED, AWSIZE=2, AWLEN=1, AWADDR=0x7FFF_0200. (3) WRAP, AWSIZE=2, AWLEN=3, AWADDR=0x7FFF_0024. (4) Single-beat INCR, AWSIZE=2, at AWADDR=0x0000_0200, so the beat address returns to the low region. The APB completer accepts every address with PREADY after 0 to 2 waits and PSLVERR=0, using an address-agnostic responder rather than the default error completer.

Unsupported reads that combine the largest size code with long declared lengths. Send these in order, with the bridge idle each time, no AW pending, and RREADY=1. (1) INCR read, ARSIZE=7 (unsupported size), ARLEN=7, ARADDR=0x0000_0000, ARCACHE=4'b0000: the bridge must return 8 SLVERR beats. (2) INCR read, ARSIZE=7, ARLEN=15, ARADDR=0x0000_0000: 16 SLVERR beats. (3) ARSIZE=6, ARLEN=15, INCR at 0x0000_0000. (4) A legal single-beat INCR read with ARSIZE=2 at 0x0000_0040, so the bridge returns to a small-size, short-length context. Take each R beat to its final RLAST handshake before the next AR is presented.

Unsupported writes that combine the largest size code with long declared lengths. Send these in order, with the bridge idle each time, no AR pending, and BREADY=1. (1) INCR write, AWSIZE=7, AWLEN=7, AWADDR=0x0000_0000, AWCACHE=4'b0000, followed by 8 W beats with WLAST on beat 7. (2) INCR write, AWSIZE=7, AWLEN=15, AWADDR=0x0000_0000, followed by 16 W beats. (3) AWSIZE=6, AWLEN=15, INCR at 0x0000_0000, with 16 W beats. (4) A legal single-beat INCR write with AWSIZE=2 at 0x0000_0040 and WSTRB=4'b1111, with the completer ready and PSLVERR=0. Wait for each B handshake before presenting the next AW.

4-KiB-crossing reads at the top of the 32-bit address space, where the end address of the burst runs past 0xFFFF_FFFF. Send these with the bridge idle, no AW pending and RREADY=1. (1) INCR read, ARSIZE=2, ARLEN=1, ARADDR=0xFFFF_FFFC, ARCACHE=4'b0000. (2) INCR read, ARSIZE=2, ARLEN=255, ARADDR=0xFFFF_FF00. Each must be rejected as a 4-KiB crossing with ARLEN+1 SLVERR beats and no APB activity. (3) A legal single-beat INCR read with ARSIZE=2 at 0x0000_0000, so the AR address presented goes back to the bottom of the address space.

4-KiB-crossing writes at the top of the 32-bit address space, where the end address of the burst runs past 0xFFFF_FFFF. Send these with the bridge idle, no AR pending and BREADY=1. (1) INCR write, AWSIZE=2, AWLEN=1, AWADDR=0xFFFF_FFFC, AWCACHE=4'b0000, followed by 2 W beats with WLAST on the second. (2) INCR write, AWSIZE=2, AWLEN=255, AWADDR=0xFFFF_FF00, followed by 256 W beats. Each must have its W beats drained, with no APB activity and one SLVERR B. (3) A legal single-beat INCR write with AWSIZE=2 at 0x0000_0000, with the completer ready and PSLVERR=0.

unreachable.reason: The size field is 3 bits wide, so the largest transfer size it can encode is 2^7 = 128 bytes, even for an unsupported size. The single-beat byte count and its low-bit mask can never reach bit 8 or above, so bits 8 to 31 are constant for every input.

Wrap-range figures are 2^(AxSIZE + log2(beats)). AxSIZE is at most 7 and the longest wrap length the spec decodes is 16 beats, so the range is at most 2^11 bytes. The wrap byte count bits 12 and up, and the matching mask bits 11 and up, never change. The AR/AW-side bits 10 and 11 are already covered.

Partly reachable. COV-103 and COV-104 cover the reachable bits: wrap byte count bits 10 and 11, and mask bits 9 and 10. The same 2^11-byte ceiling (AxSIZE <= 7, at most 16 decoded beats) keeps wrap byte count bits 12 to 31 at 0 and mask bits 11 to 31 at 1.
The total burst length is at most 256 beats times 128 bytes (largest encodable size) = 2^15 bytes. Total-byte bits 16 to 32 can never be set by any input.
The wrap length code covers only 2, 4, 8 and 16 beats, so its log2 value is at most 4. Bit 3 of that code is never set.
Partly reachable. COV-101 and COV-102 cover the reachable bits, 16 to 30 (bit 31 is already covered). PADDR bits [1:0] must always be 0 (word alignment, CHK-004), so those bits cannot toggle.

The bridge returns only OKAY (2'b00) or SLVERR (2'b10) on B and R. It never returns DECERR, and it cannot return EXOKAY because exclusive access is not implemented. Bit 0 of BRESP/RRESP is therefore always 0.
